name: Telenor Svalbard Longyearbyen headquarters and data center
notes: Telenor press release says the rebuilt Longyearbyen office and data center was taken into use in March 2022, has rooftop solar producing up to 30-33 kW peak and up to 30000 kWh/year, and uses data center waste heat for the office building. No IT load/MW capacity disclosed.

name: KSAT SvalSat Platåfjellet data center
notes: JM Hansen project page lists KSAT as client, 1400 m2 area, year 2024-, and says a new data center is being established on Platåfjellet to meet increased data capacity and reliability needs at SvalSat. KSAT source confirms Svalbard Ground Station has high-speed fibre backhaul and delivers data with Gbit capacity into cloud or to customers. No MW capacity disclosed.

name: Arctic World Archive
developer: Piql and Store Norske Spitsbergen Kulkompani (SNSK)
notes: Specialized offline/cold data preservation facility in Mine no. 3 near Longyearbyen, opened in 2017. DCD described it as a Svalbard data center located 300m deep in permafrost and storing Piql film; AWA official site describes a Svalbard vault for physical and digital security. Not a conventional colocation/hyperscale compute site; no MW capacity disclosed.

name: Arctic Way Jan Mayen and Longyearbyen cable landing stations
developer: Space Norway; SubCom; Forsvarsbygg support on Jan Mayen
notes: Digital-infrastructure adjacent rather than a compute data center: Space Norway says the Jan Mayen cable landing station is under construction/support works for the Arctic Way subsea fibre system, with landing stations in Bodo, Jan Mayen, and Longyearbyen and planned completion in 2028. Included because it is a named station project supporting critical Arctic data connectivity; no data center MW capacity.
